newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close mixed as New York soars.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close mixed as New York soars.

* Toronto stock market's key index ended higher in light dealings, following Wall Street's rise despite weakness in key golds. * Declines edged advances 506 to 497. * Bre-X fell.
Toronto stocks ended mixed in light dealings on Monday, pulled in conflicting directions by a stronger Wall Street and bank issues, and slipping golds and forestry products.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 15.57 points to 6242.42, just shy of its life-time high of 6260.73 reached on February 19.
Declining issues inched ahead of advances 506 to 497, while 277 traded unchanged. New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 76.58 points to 7008.20, aided by strength in high-technology stocks.
Gains in Toronto's 300 index were led by the weighty banking sector, which rose 0.8 percent, said Calgary-based portfolio manager Josef Schachter. "It was a blue-chip rally in Canada."
The nation's biggest banks will report first-quarter earnings starting on Tuesday, led by fourth-ranked Bank of Nova Scotia and third-ranked Bank of Montreal.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indices gained ground including consumer products, pipelines, banks and conglomerates. The four weaker ones were golds, forestry products, retail and transportation.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd extended Friday's losses, dropping 1.40 to 19.80 on almost 3.7 million shares. Part of the slide stemmed from Friday's news that Placer Dome Inc was no longer interested in bidding for the prospector.
Bre-X announced a deal with Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc last week and investors struggled to place a value for the Calgary company.
* Forest products heavyweight MacMillan Bloedel Ltd eased 0.25 to 19.05 on a block of seven million shares.
